expected_evidence: Continuous, annually-resolved ice-core stratigraphy from Greenland cores (GISP2, GRIP, NGRIP) spanning the YD onset, including layer-counted chronologies (e.g., GICC05) that could show ambiguity or revision in the exact date of onset
Cosmogenic radionuclide records (10Be in ice, 14C in tree rings/speleothems) used as independent chronometers to cross-check ice-core layer counts and reveal dating discrepancies

Marine and terrestrial meltwater-pulse proxies (sea-level jump records, coral reef terraces, foraminiferal/oxygen-isotope shifts) associated with MWP-1A that could be compared against the ice-core YD onset date to test synchroneity or lag
Varve-count and lake-sediment chronologies (e.g., European lake records) offering alternate absolute dating that might conflict with or support ice-core ages
Speleothem U-series dated records showing abrupt hydroclimate shifts near YD onset, useful for chronological cross-validation
Published glaciological/geochronological literature explicitly discussing dating uncertainty, offset, or inconclusiveness between meltwater-pulse timing and YD cooling onset in Greenland records
Model-prior consensus estimate (~12,900-12,850 cal BP for YD onset) against which the claimed wide 'inconclusive' interval (extending anomalously to ~5950) would be evaluated
response.rationale: The hypothesis is a meta-claim about dating uncertainty between a meltwater pulse and the Younger Dryas onset as recorded in the Greenland ice sheet, so the relevant evidence kinds are geological (ice-core stratigraphy, varves, speleothems) and astronomical/geochronological (cosmogenic nuclide chronologies used for cross-dating), with some material (marine/coral sea-level proxies) support. No period tag was supplied, but the subject matter spans the younger-dryas/early-holocene boundary, where the table gives geological ≈0.6-0.65 and astronomical ≈0.65-0.7 — both comparatively high-detectability channels, reflecting that ice cores, cosmogenic isotope records, and sediment archives are physically robust, still exist, and are actively studied and re-dated in the literature. Textual, linguistic, and oral-tradition evidence are essentially inapplicable/undetectable (~0-0.15) for this pre-literate, purely physical-proxy timeframe, so their absence is fully expected and uninformative about truth or falsity. Because the core evidence types (ice-core layers, cosmogenic isotopes, marine/sediment proxies) have good preservation and are routinely reported in peer-reviewed glaciology/paleoclimate literature, genuine dating-uncertainty debates about YD onset synchroneity with meltwater pulses are plausible to find if they exist — detectability is moderate-to-good, not the limiting factor. However, the anomalously wide claimed interval (extending to ~5950, well into the Holocene, far past any mainstream YD-onset estimate) is not something dating uncertainty in ice cores would plausibly produce; this stretches credulity independent of detectability and should be weighed as evidence against the hypothesis as stated, even though the underlying evidence classes are well-preserved and searchable. I set a blended detectability adjustment of 0.55, averaging the moderately-high geological/astronomical scores against the near-zero scores for textual/linguistic/oral channels that are structurally inapplicable to this ice-sheet/paleoclimate context.
